q: 391. Pile foundations are usually provided for .............
explain: Pile foundations are commonly used for high-rise multistoreyed buildings to transfer heavy loads to deeper, stronger strata.

q: 392. Number of piles required to support a column .............
explain: Per the reference key, a minimum group of 3 piles is generally used under a column to ensure stability and avoid eccentricity issues with fewer piles.

q: 393. Under reamed piles are generally .............
explain: Under-reamed piles are a type of bored (cast-in-situ) pile with an enlarged base, formed by drilling rather than driving.

q: 394. Consolidation is generally considered to be a function of .............
explain: Consolidation behaviour (compression) is governed by changes in effective stress, per Terzaghi's principle.

q: 395. In the Terzaghi's theory of one dimensional consolidation it is assumed that .............
options: coefficient of volume change is not constant
explain: A core assumption of Terzaghi's theory is that both flow and compression occur strictly in one dimension (vertical).

q: 396. The unit of the coefficient of consolidation is .............
explain: Coefficient of consolidation Cv has units of area per time, i.e., cm2/sec.

q: 397. Tunneling is required in case of .............
explain: Tunneling is specifically employed to create an underground passage, distinct from surface construction.

q: 398. The most suitable soil for compressed air tunneling is .............
explain: Per the reference key, silt is marked as most suitable for compressed air tunneling in this classification.

q: 399. In a compressed air tunneling, the volume of free air provided is .............
options: 6 m3 per second per m2 of face area
6 m3 per minute per m2 of face area
20 m3 per minute per m2 of face area
6 m3 per hour per m2 of face area
explain: Standard practice for compressed air tunneling supplies free air at a rate of about 6 m3 per minute per m2 of tunnel face area.

q: 400. The entrance of tunnel is called .............
explain: The entrance/opening of a tunnel is termed the portal.

q: 401. Amount of energy released by an earthquake is called .............
explain: Magnitude is the standard measure of the total energy released at an earthquake's source.

q: 402. Instrument used to measure earthquake is .............
explain: A seismograph is the instrument used to detect and record ground motion during earthquakes.

q: 403. At convergent plate boundaries, one would expect to find .............
explain: Convergent boundaries, where plates collide and compress, produce both folding and faulting of rock strata.

q: 404. At divergent plate boundaries, one would expect to find .............
explain: Divergent boundaries, where plates pull apart under tension, primarily produce normal faults rather than folds.

q: 405. The point where movement occurred which triggered the earthquake is the .............
explain: The focus (hypocenter) is the actual underground point where fault rupture and earthquake energy release originates.

q: 406. Which of the following sequences correctly lists the different arrivals from first to last?
explain: P waves travel fastest, followed by slower S waves, with surface waves (slowest) arriving last.

q: 407. Drift method of tunneling is used to construct tunnels in .............
explain: The drift method, involving excavation of a small pilot tunnel first, is typically used in rock formations.

q: 408. In full face method of constructing tunnels, the first operation relates to .............
options: excavation of one drift in the center
excavation being done along the periphery
explain: The full face method begins with excavating a central pilot drift, which is then enlarged outward to the full tunnel section.

q: 409. Which one of the following is a component of a shield for tunneling?
explain: The cutting edge is a key structural component of a tunneling shield, used to cut into the ground as the shield advances.

q: 410. Which of the following describes the build up and release of stress during an earthquake?
explain: Elastic rebound theory explains how strain energy accumulates in rock and is suddenly released as an earthquake when the rock ruptures.

q: 411. The amount of ground displacement in an earthquake is called .............
explain: Slip refers to the relative displacement of rock on either side of a fault during an earthquake.

q: 412. The two sides of folds are called its .............
explain: The two flanks/sides of a geological fold are called its limbs.

q: 413. Which two measurements describe the orientation of a fault plane at a given location?
explain: Strike (compass direction of the fault line) and dip (angle of inclination) together fully describe a fault plane's orientation.

q: 414. Nepal lies in seismic zone .............
explain: Nepal lies within the highest seismic hazard zone (Zone V) due to its position along the active Himalayan collision boundary.

q: 415. How do rock particles move during the passage of a P wave through the rock?
options: Back and forth parallel to the direction of wave travel
Back and forth perpendicular to the direction of wave travel
explain: P (primary/compressional) waves cause particle motion parallel to the direction of wave propagation, like a push-pull motion.

q: 416. How many seismograph stations are needed to locate the epicenter of an earthquake?
explain: At least three seismograph stations are needed to triangulate and pinpoint an earthquake's epicenter location.

q: 417. Earthquakes can occur with ............. faulting.
explain: Earthquakes can be generated by normal, reverse, or thrust faulting, depending on the tectonic stress regime.

q: 418. Which of the following lining material is useful for shield driven tunnels in sub aqueous regions?
explain: Cast iron segments provide strong, watertight lining suited for shield-driven tunnels under rivers or water bodies.

q: 419. Which of the following measures an earthquake's intensity based on the observed effects on people and structures?
explain: The Modified Mercalli scale measures earthquake intensity based on observed effects on people, objects, and structures, unlike the energy-based Richter/moment magnitude scales.

q: 420. In Belgium method of tunneling .............
options: construction of side walls is completed before invert and roof arch are built
construction of roof arch is completed before side walls and invert are built
construction of invert is completed before side walls and roof arch are built
construction of invert and side walls is completed before roof arch is built
explain: In the Belgian method, the roof arch is constructed first, providing support before the side walls and invert are excavated and built below.

q: 421. Approximately what percentage of earthquakes occur at plate boundaries?
explain: The vast majority (about 90%) of earthquakes occur along tectonic plate boundaries where stress accumulates from relative plate motion.

q: 422. Vibrations radiate from focus in all directions as .............
explain: Ground vibrations from an earthquake's focus radiate outward in all directions as seismic waves (comprising both P and S body waves).

q: 423. The moment of magnitude of earthquake depends on all of the following except .............
options: the area of the fault break
explain: Moment magnitude is calculated from fault rupture area, rock rigidity, and slip distance; the specific type of faulting (normal/reverse/thrust) is not a direct input.

q: 424. Circular section of tunnel is not suitable for .............
explain: Per the reference key, circular sections are marked as unsuitable for concrete lining placement in this context, though they are otherwise structurally efficient and widely used with shield methods.

q: 425. A good blast with a good yield is obtained if the cut hole is .............
explain: A shallow-angled cut hole (around 15° to the face) is used to create an effective free face for a good blasting yield.

q: 426. Earthquakes occur more frequently at .............
explain: Plate boundaries, where tectonic stress concentrates from relative plate movement, are the most frequent sites of earthquake activity.

q: 427. Where do most earthquakes occur?
explain: Most earthquakes occur along faults, where accumulated tectonic stress is released through sudden rock rupture and slip.

q: 428. If D is the diameter of tunnel in meters, then the thickness of lining in mm as per the empirical formula is given by .............
explain: The empirical formula for tunnel lining thickness commonly used is t = 104D (in mm), where D is the tunnel diameter in meters.

q: 429. Which one of the following tunneling methods is used for laying underground sewers?
explain: The Italian method of tunneling is traditionally associated with constructing underground sewer tunnels.

q: 430. Ribs are used for strengthening and stiffening the liner plate for tunnels of diameter greater than .............
explain: For tunnels with diameter greater than about 3 m, additional steel ribs are used to reinforce and stiffen the liner plates.

q: 431. As compared to a single free face, if a charge of explosive is placed equidistant from two faces, then the yield .............
explain: A charge placed between two free faces benefits from reduced resistance on both sides, increasing blast yield by roughly 2.25 times compared to a single free face.

q: 432. Drifters can be used to drill .............
explain: Drifter drills are versatile machines capable of drilling horizontal, downward, and upward blast holes in tunneling operations.

q: 433. If N is the number of shafts used, then the total number of faces available for attacking the excavation and construction in tunnels are .............
explain: Each shaft provides two working faces (in both directions along the tunnel), plus two additional faces from the tunnel's own portals, giving 2N+2 total faces.

q: 434. The correct sequence of drilling equipment for increasing size of holes in tunnels is .............
options: wagon drill, churn drill, shot drill
wagon drill, shot drill, churn drill
shot drill, churn drill, wagon drill
churn drill, wagon drill, shot drill
explain: Per standard tunneling practice, hole sizes progressively increase using wagon drill, then shot drill, then churn drill equipment.

q: 435. Which of the following is not a component of the shield?
explain: Liner plates form the permanent tunnel lining installed behind the shield, not a structural component of the shield itself (which includes hood, jacks, and tail).

q: 436. Who developed the procedure used to measure the size of an earthquake?
explain: Charles Richter developed the original magnitude scale used to quantify the size (energy) of earthquakes.

q: 437. If an S wave were to go from a solid to a liquid-what would happen to its velocity?
explain: S waves require shear rigidity to propagate, and liquids cannot support shear stress, so an S wave's velocity drops to zero entering a liquid.

q: 438. Body waves consists of .............
explain: Body waves, which travel through the Earth's interior, consist of both P (compressional) and S (shear) waves.

q: 439. In general, the most destructive earthquakes waves are the .............
explain: Surface waves, with their larger amplitude and lower frequency near the ground surface, generally cause the most structural damage.

q: 440. How do particles move during the passage of a S wave through the rock?
options: Back and forth parallel to the direction of wave travel
Perpendicular to the direction of wave travel
explain: S (shear) waves cause particle motion perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation.

q: 441. How do particles move during the passage of a P wave through the rock?
options: Back and forth parallel to the direction of wave travel
Perpendicular to the direction of wave travel
explain: P (compressional) waves move particles back and forth parallel to the direction the wave is traveling.

q: 442. The maximum angle of slope of a bed with horizontal is known as .............
explain: Dip is defined as the maximum angle of inclination of a rock bed measured from the horizontal.

q: 443. Geographic direction of intersection of the bedding plane with a horizontal plane is called .............
explain: Strike is the compass direction of the line formed by the intersection of a bedding (or fault) plane with a horizontal plane.

q: 444. Which of the following is true in relation to apparent and true dip?
explain: Apparent dip, measured on any section not perpendicular to strike, is always less than or equal to the true dip; strictly it is always <= true dip, and generally less.

q: 445. Which of the following methods of tunneling is used for long tunnels at great depths?
explain: The Austrian (New Austrian Tunneling Method) is suited for long tunnels at great depths, using the surrounding rock mass itself for support.

q: 446. The bulk modulus measures .............
options: the resistance to flow of a liquid
the resistance to change in color
the resistance to change in volume
the resistance to change in shape
explain: Bulk modulus quantifies a material's resistance to uniform compression, i.e., resistance to volume change under pressure.

q: 447. If a P wave were to go from a solid to a liquid ............. what would happen to its velocity?
explain: P waves travel more slowly through liquids than through solids because liquids have lower rigidity, so velocity decreases at a solid-liquid boundary.

q: 448. Which of the following waves is the slowest?
explain: Per the reference key this is marked 'P waves'; the standard seismological fact is that P waves are actually the fastest, and surface waves are the slowest of the seismic wave types.

q: 449. A syncline is a fold in which .............
options: the younger rocks usually occupy a position in the interior
explain: A syncline is a downward (trough-shaped) fold where younger rock layers occupy the innermost, core position.

q: 450. The head of the fault plane is its inclination with the .............
explain: Per the reference key, the 'hade' (inclination from vertical) of a fault plane is measured relative to the vertical.

q: 451. The bottom floor of tunnel is called .............
explain: The invert is the term for the bottom floor (base) of a tunnel.

q: 452. Which thrust line has highest potentiality of largest earthquake in Nepal?
explain: The Main Central Thrust (MCT) is identified in this reference as having the highest potential for generating the largest earthquakes in Nepal.

q: 453. In the field, coarse grained soils and fine grained soils are distinguished based on .............
options: appearance of individual grains to the naked eye
explain: In the field, coarse-grained and fine-grained soils are distinguished simply by whether individual grains are visible to the naked eye.
